conclusion.justification: The report highlights that the highest-quality, independent evidence (such as Cochrane reviews and placebo-controlled meta-analyses) finds no reliable benefit over placebo, concluding that current evidence does not convincingly support ginkgo as an effective tinnitus treatment despite some conflicting, lower-quality or industry-linked studies.
conclusion.label: leans_reject

report:
## Conclusion

The evidence on Ginkgo biloba extract for tinnitus is **mixed and inconclusive**, with the most rigorous, independent evidence (Cochrane) finding **no reliable benefit** over placebo.

- The **Cochrane systematic review** (the gold-standard for evidence synthesis) concluded there is no reliable evidence that ginkgo reduces tinnitus severity compared to placebo ([cochranelibrary.com](https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD004407.pub4/full); summarized at [earlabs.app](https://earlabs.app/articles/ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus-evidence/)).
- A randomized placebo-controlled trial combined with a meta-analysis of randomized trials by Rejali et al. similarly concluded that "Ginkgo biloba does not benefit patients with tinnitus" ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36383762](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36383762/)).
- In contrast, a systematic review of the standardized extract EGb 761® reported that all eight identified randomized, placebo-controlled trials showed statistically significant superiority over placebo, concluding EGb 761® is an "evidence-based" option ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3157487](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3157487/)).
- Newer studies, including a 2025 exploratory open-label trial of 170 patients on EGb 761®, reported symptomatic improvement, but this was uncontrolled (no placebo arm), limiting causal conclusions ([mdpi.com/2077-0383/15/1/87](https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0383/15/1/87)).

**Bottom line:** Results depend heavily on which studies are included and how "benefit" is measured. Industry-linked reviews of the specific EGb 761® formulation report benefit, but the independent Cochrane review and an independent randomized trial/meta-analysis found no reliable benefit over placebo. Given the higher methodological weight typically given to Cochrane reviews, current evidence does not convincingly support ginkgo as an effective tinnitus treatment, though some may experience modest relief with the standardized EGb 761® extract. Consult a physician before use, especially given bleeding-risk interactions with ginkgo.
